observation_summary: The StringUtils.join method throws a NullPointerException when an object in the array has a toString() method that returns null, because the initial capacity calculation for the StringBuilder attempts to call .length() on that null result.
reasoning_summary: The fix replaces an incorrect algorithm for calculating the initial capacity of the StringBuilder (which relied on the toString() result of the first element) with a more robust, safe estimation (noOfItems * 16). This is a correction of the implementation logic for efficiency/correctness, fitting the Algorithm/Method definition.
evidence_used: The fix changes the StringBuilder initialization from (array[startIndex] == null ? 16 : array[startIndex].toString().length()) + 1 to noOfItems * 16.
The bug report states that the NPE occurs when toString() returns null.
The stack trace confirms the NPE occurs at the line where the StringBuilder is initialized.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix avoids an NPE, it does so by changing the algorithm used to estimate capacity rather than simply adding a null check to validate the input.
The fix is not just about initializing a variable, but about changing the logic/algorithm used to determine the capacity of a data structure.
